# Clipper CLI

Inspect planned file updates without touching your filesystem.

## Requirements

- Node 22+

## CLI Example

```sh
$ clipper dry-run ./in
```

## Behavior Summary

The `dry-run` subcommand takes an input directory (`./in`) and simulates processing so you can review proposed changes ahead of time. Because it is read-only, `clipper dry-run ./in` never writes files to disk.

## Exit Codes

- `0`: Preview succeeded without errors.
- Non-zero: Failed to inspect `./in` or encountered an execution error.

# Clipper

CLI for previewing changes safely before writing to disk.

## Prerequisites

- Node 22 runtime

## Usage Example

```sh
clipper dry-run ./in
```

## Behavior Summary

`clipper dry-run ./in` requires Node 22 and previews the changes it would apply to `./in` without writing any files. It exits with `0` on success and a non-zero exit code if execution fails.

## Exit Status Notes

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `0` | Preview succeeded with no files written |
| Non-zero | Command failed |
